We derive the scalar tidal Love numbers analytically for both classes of modes and show that their dissipative parts exhibit distinct low-frequency behavior, reflecting whether one or both potential barriers participate in the scattering process. We further find that, as the wormhole approaches the black-hole limit, the super-throat contribution becomes progressively negligible, while the sub-throat response smoothly reduces to that of a Schwarzschild black hole. These results demonstrate that the tidal response of wormholes depends crucially on whether the perturbation probes the global structure of the throat.
item.dc:creator: Sergey N. Solodukhin, Vagif Tagiev

item.title: Thermodynamic Representations of Algebraically Modified FLRW Dynamics at the Apparent Horizon
item.description: arXiv:2609.13720v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic description of a general class of algebraically modified Friedmann dynamics in which the physical matter obeys the standard conservation equation and the modification is encoded through a function \(g(\rho)\). By introducing a thermodynamic matter representation \(\chi(\rho)\), we construct the corresponding matter variables, heat flow, work term, and horizon entropy, and show that both the Clausius relation and the first-law balance can be consistently maintained. A continuous family of representations is then defined by \(\chi_\lambda(\rho)=(1-\lambda)\rho+\lambda g(\rho)\) with \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\), and the physical-matter and effective-fluid descriptions as the two endpoints. The associated thermodynamic quantities transform consistently between these limits. We further show that apparent departures from equilibrium can arise from mixing quantities belonging to different representations, rather than from a genuine non-equilibrium entropy-production mechanism. These results identify a continuous freedom of thermodynamic representation within this class of modified FLRW dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Liu

item.title: Periodic Orbits of Van der Waals Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2609.15278v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Black holes in asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime whose extended-phase-space thermodynamics reproduces that of a van der Waals fluid exactly form a distinctive class, the van der Waals black holes (VBHs). The timelike geodesics of VBHs are solved, their periodic orbits are catalogued, and the gravitational waves emitted along them are computed, so as to trace how the thermodynamic pressure P and the molecular-volume parameter b shape the orbital dynamics. Integrating the geodesic equations numerically yields the energy, angular momentum and radius of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and maps out the family of bound orbits. To delimit the parameter window in which the effective potential stays well behaved, we introduce a critical angular momentum Ls. Within the orbit-classification scheme, we compute the energies corresponding to rational q for several parameter sets and display the resulting orbits. The waveforms produced along these orbits are generated within the "Kludge" formalism, which makes it possible to quantify the imprint of b on the wave amplitude and on the period. Both the orbital architecture and the gravitational-wave signature turn out to be strongly sensitive to b. The dynamical behavior of VBHs and Schwarzschild-AdS (SAdS) black holes differs markedly, providing a new perspective for probing black hole thermodynamics via gravitational wave observations.
item.dc:creator: Xuyao Gong, Zhaoyi Xu, Meirong Tang

item.title: Jordan-like invariant representations of scalar-tensor gravity and the return of imperfect-fluid thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2609.20189v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It has been shown that the thermodynamics of frame-invariant scalar-tensor gravity admits an Einstein-frame-like invariant representation, in which the scalar sector is minimally coupled and behaves as a perfect fluid with vanishing temperature. We show that this is not the only invariant thermodynamic organization available. Using instead the invariant matter metric, we construct a Jordan-frame-like invariant representation in which matter is minimally coupled and the gravitational action takes the Brans-Dicke-Bergmann-Wagoner form with invariant fields $\Psi=\mathcal I_1^{-1}$, $\mathcal U(\Psi)$, and $\omega_{\mathrm{inv}}(\Psi)$. In this representation the metric field equations retain the Hessian sector characteristic of Jordan-frame scalar-tensor gravity. A $1+3$ decomposition of the corresponding effective stress tensor yields nonvanishing heat flux and anisotropic stress in a generic congruence. In the $\Psi$-comoving frame, the usual first-order thermodynamic identifications are recovered in invariant form, including $K_{\mathrm J}T_{\mathrm J}=-\dot\Psi/(\kappa^2\Psi)$ and $\eta_{\mathrm J}=\dot\Psi/(2\kappa^2\Psi)$, with the bulk channel obtained in homogeneous and isotropic sectors. Thus, frame-invariant scalar-tensor thermodynamics is not intrinsically restricted to an Einstein-frame-like perfect-fluid description: it also admits a Jordan-frame-like invariant formulation in which the effective imperfect-fluid interpretation is manifest.
item.dc:creator: David S. Pereira, Jos\'e Pedro Mimoso

item.title: Constraining the Quadratic-mode Amplitude Coupling in GW250114
item.description: arXiv:2609.28953v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Detecting quadratic quasi-normal modes in black hole ringdowns would provide evidence for nonlinear gravitational dynamics, while measuring their properties would enable tests of the corresponding predictions of general relativity. Specifically, second-order black hole perturbation theory predicts that their amplitudes scale with the product of the amplitudes of their parent linear modes, with a coupling coefficient that depends on the spin of the remnant black hole. This mode-specific coupling coefficient has not yet been directly measured from gravitational wave data. Here, we use Bayesian inference on the GW250114 ringdown, modeled with the $220$, $221$, and $220\times220$ modes, to infer the amplitude-coupling coefficient of the $220\times220$ mode. The inferred coefficient is consistent with predictions from numerical relativity fits and second-order perturbation theory; no comparison shows a deviation exceeding $1.3 \sigma$. Although the current data cannot distinguish among these spin-dependent predictions, this measurement establishes a basis for more stringent observational tests of nonlinear gravitational dynamics in black-hole ringdowns.
item.dc:creator: Yuxin Yang, Changfu Shi, Yi-Ming Hu

item.title: Optimal Strategies for Gravitational-Wave Memory Detection with Noise Marginalization in Pulsar Timing Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2610.20772v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Current pulsar timing arrays could detect gravitational wave memory, which would provide a unique test of general relativity. In order to optimize our searches for gravitational wave memory in pulsar timing arrays, we integrate the optimal frequentist statistics for GW memory into the \texttt{enterprise} code suite. We additionally test a noise marginalized version of this statistic, and compare it's effectiveness to the simpler maximum posterior method. We perform these tests on simulated pulsar timing array with red and white noise content, as well as the NANOGrav $15$-year data set. We find no significant variations in our detection statistics between the noise-marginalized and the maximum-posterior methods for the simulated datasets, and only small variations in the NANOGrav $15$-year comparisons. We conclude that for realistic PTAs the noise-marginalization method could be useful for assigning a false alarm probability to Bayesian results, though the maximum posterior method is sufficient for identifying potentially detectable signals.
item.dc:creator: Rand Burnette, Xavier Siemens

item.title: Rotation slows the instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29941v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rotation weakens the radial instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in slow-rotation perturbation theory. We investigate its nonlinear effect by evolving stationary rotating drainholes supported by a phantom scalar field. We construct the backgrounds with an independent spectral solver, validate them against published symmetric solutions, and identify a misprint in a published field equation that did not affect the original authors' numerical results. Evolutions perturbed only by discretization error show that rotation slows the collapse. At intermediate spins some throats expand, with the direction of departure depending on the effective perturbation. At the fastest evolved spin, the throat's areal radius shows no growing departure through evolution time $t=150$ in code units, about 28 e-folding times of the static instability, at three resolutions. Two other rapidly rotating models also show no growth over their reliable evolution intervals. Collapsing rotating throats emit an axisymmetric quadrupolar gravitational-wave burst whose energy increases between the two spins compared. Second-order initial data excite the instability through their background truncation error. The results establish slower collapse and prolonged absence of detected radial growth for the sampled asymmetric backgrounds, over finite times from initially axisymmetric data.
item.dc:creator: Nikita M. Shirokov, Ilya Nachevsky

item.title: The Symbiosis of Vainshtein and Chameleon Screening
item.description: arXiv:2610.36166v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first study of coexisting Vainshtein and Chameleon screening in cosmic structures. Screening hides fifth forces locally, keeping modified gravity viable. Realistic dark-energy models can activate several mechanisms at once, yet this interplay has been overlooked. We find that (i) the Chameleon resolves the longstanding Galileon void pathology; (ii) it suppresses or eliminates the Vainshtein radius around massive sources; and (iii) the Vainshtein term shrinks the Chameleon's screened core. These effects reshape the observable signatures central to cosmological tests of gravity.
item.dc:creator: Sergi Sirera, Tessa Baker, Clare Burrage, James Hallam, Krishna Naidoo

item.title: Isospectrality breaking in the axial quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.38742v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study odd-parity perturbations of Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity. The dCS action is parity invariant because $\vartheta\,{}^{*}RR$ is the product of two pseudoscalars; nevertheless, the pseudoscalar perturbation has odd parity and enters only the axial sector at linear order and so lifts the axial--polar isospectrality of general relativity. We derive the finite-charge couplings between the pseudoscalar and the axial gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations directly from the linearized field equations. Both directions are governed by the radial kernel $(Mr-Q^2)\Delta/r^8$, and at nonzero charge the pseudoscalar couples to $\Psi+\chi\Psi_e$, with $\chi=2Q/[r\sqrt{(l-1)(l+2)}]$. After diagonalizing the Einstein--Maxwell sector, we compute branch-resolved quasinormal-mode shifts with exterior complex scaling for the photon-sphere modes and Frobenius shooting for the near-extremal zero-damping modes. For the Schwarzschild $l=2$ fundamental mode we obtain $\beta\,\delta\omega=-0.7733-0.3946\,i$ (units $M=\alpha=1$). Off resonance, the gravitational-led shift scales as $\zeta\,l^3$ at $Q=0$ but as $\zeta\,l^2/Q$ at fixed nonzero charge and large $l$. The electromagnetic-led branch becomes exactly degenerate with the pseudoscalar mode at $Q_c=2M\sqrt{l(l+1)+1}/[l(l+1)+2]$, where the pseudoscalar potential coincides with the polar partner of the electromagnetic-led potential; there the breaking is $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt\zeta)$, $M|\Delta\omega|\simeq2.4\sqrt\zeta$ for $l=2$, and the shift reverses sign across $Q_c$. Near extremality the photon-sphere shifts remain finite, whereas the non-degenerate fundamental gravitational-led zero-damping mode is suppressed, $\delta\omega/\omega\simeq6.0\times10^{3}\,\zeta\,(1-Q^2/M^2)$ for $l=2$.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Rout

item.title: Quasi-equilibrium tidal folds of white dwarfs around rotating black holes in shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). The relativistic tidal field is obtained from numerical EsGB backgrounds in a parallel-transported frame and coupled to a compressible affine model. Comparisons with Kerr black holes matched in Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass and angular momentum show a positive shift in the orbital frequency at the tidal fold. At fixed spin the relative correction follows an approximately quadratic dependence on the EsGB coupling, consistent with the leading response of the metric to the scalar field. Over the sampled backgrounds, the relative correction reaches order $10^{-3}$. Black hole rotation also changes the relation between the tidal fold and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO): the sampled prograde folds remain outside the ISCO, while retrograde folds move inside it at higher spins. Orbital orientation therefore controls whether tidal equilibrium is lost before the orbital stability limit is reached. For the stellar and black hole masses considered here, the characteristic gravitational wave (GW) frequencies fall in the millihertz band relevant to planned space based interferometers. Future GW observations capable of resolving deviations from Kerr predictions could constrain the EsGB coupling.
item.dc:creator: Shoupan Liu, Meilin Liu, Yu Wang, Yunqi Liu, Bin Wang

item.title: Matter Spectral Functions from Quantum Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2507.17862v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate Lorentzian quantum gravity coupled to a template matter sector with gauge fields, scalars and fermions. In the absence of quantised gravity, the matter sector by itself is renormalisable, but UV-incomplete. Provided quantum gravity offers an asymptotically safe UV-completion, we determine the photon and scalar two-point functions in the presence of gravitational fluctuations, and show that both possess a K\"all\'en-Lehmann spectral representation. Our results are achieved using functional renormalisation adapted for theories in Lorentzian signature. We explain why and how interactions with gravity modify both the infrared as well as the ultraviolet behaviour of matter spectral functions. We further determine the corresponding form factors on the level of the quantum effective action. Limitations and extensions of our study are discussed alongside implications for particle physics and unitarity of quantum gravity with matter.
item.dc:creator: Varun Kher, Brandon King, Daniel F. Litim, Manuel Reichert

item.title: How Significant are Cosmological Collider Signals in the Planck Data?
item.description: arXiv:2511.17500v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The search for primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) is theoretically well motivated but remains observationally challenging. Tight constraints with low significance for the standard non-Gaussian shapes suggest that detection may lie beyond the reach of near-future experiments. However, tests of PNG are highly template-dependent. From a theory perspective, a whole new family of bispectrum shapes arise in the cosmological collider program, with distinct signatures of heavy particles during inflation. In this work, we provide a class of simplified collider templates for these particles that encompasses a broader range of masses, sound speeds, and interactions. We propose that, given the current state of observations, the most effective strategy to search for PNG signals is through orthogonalizing the collider templates, such that they are uncorrelated with the tightly constrained single field predictions. Our results show that removing the single-field contribution enhances the signal across all four templates studied. Using the {\it Modal} pipeline and \textit{Planck} CMB data, we perform a systematic parameter scan of the (\textit{orthogonalized}) collider templates with the most significant result reaching $2.4\sigma$ for spin-0, after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect; indicative results for spin-1 and spin-2 peak around 2$\sigma$. These results indicate that, with refined collider templates and improved data analysis strategies, there are credible prospects with forthcoming observations to detect PNG {\it and also} identify the presence of massive particles during inflation.
item.dc:creator: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E. P. S. Shellard

item.title: Kinetic magnetohydrodynamics and Landau fluid closure in relativity
item.description: arXiv:2604.05058v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffuse accretion flows near a supermassive black hole are fundamentally weakly collisional. In such weakly collisional plasmas, the ion and electron distribution functions can deviate significantly from thermal equilibrium, and particle kinetic effects can influence large-scale fluid motion by driving pressure anisotropy, heat conduction, and plasma instabilities. Modeling these plasma effects in highly relativistic flows could be important for interpreting horizon-scale observations of black hole images. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas in general relativity by deriving the relativistic drift kinetic equations from the Vlasov-Maxwell equations. We present the evolution equations for the moments of the gyroaveraged distribution function and introduce a new analytic Landau fluid closure to capture anisotropic heat flow in relativistic plasmas. Unlike standard (collisional) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics or extended magnetohydrodynamics, our model does not rely on strong collisions to enforce thermal equilibrium and consistently incorporates Landau damping in a fluid closure. The model introduced in this work provides a complementary approach to fully kinetic simulations in understanding weakly collisional effects in low-luminosity relativistic black hole accretion disks.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Hegade K. R., James M. Stone

item.title: Some universalities in the partition functions of low-dimensional gravity models
item.description: arXiv:2605.25251v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, first, we discuss the connections between various low-dimensional quantum gravity models, including 3d Chern-Simons, 2d Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT), 2d background field (BF) theory, 2d Liouville, 2d Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW), and 1d Schwarzian, which are related through holography and dimension reduction, and discuss some universalities in their partition functions. Then, we specifically examine the JT partition function and the partition function of $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ on $S^2$ and $\text{AdS}_2$ and discuss their similarities and therefore examine our proposed universalities. We change the parameters in each model and based on the change in the structure of the partition functions, strengthen our conjectures. We also use eigenfunctions, spectra and the behaviors of Wheeler-DeWitt wavefunctions to generate more universalities between these low-dimensional quantum gravity models, specifically in their partition functions. Finally, we use entanglement entropy, complexity and RG flows, particularly in the context of wormholes, to find more universalities in quantum gravity models.
item.dc:creator: Mahdis Ghodrati

item.title: Cancellation of one-loop time dependence in superhorizon curvature perturbations from all scales
item.description: arXiv:2606.28247v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show the conservation of the superhorizon curvature perturbations at one-loop level in spatially-flat gauge, including contributions from loop wavenumbers on all scales in the decoupling limit, $\epsilon (\equiv -\dot H/H^2) \to 0$. In contrast to previous works, we do not assume a hierarchy $k \gg q$ between the wavenumber of the loop integral, $k$, and that of the power spectrum, $q$, and we explicitly include the regime $k \lesssim q$. Taking into account the nonlinear relation between the inflaton fluctuation and the curvature perturbation with the $\delta N$ formalism, we show that the apparent time dependence of the one-loop curvature power spectrum cancels once all contributions, including boundary terms, are combined consistently.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Inomata

item.title: Poisson bracket and $L_\infty$ algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.30630v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the Poisson bracket of a Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. If the symplectic structure on phase space is defined following recent work, we show that the Poisson bracket can be computed with the Peierls formula, confirming the well-known result of the covariant phase space formalism. Of particular interest is the Poisson bracket in nonlocal theories. In $p$-adic string theory we find that a straightforward construction of the Poisson bracket is obstructed by higher derivative instabilities. We also discuss the inverse relation between the Poisson bracket and symplectic structure in the language of homological algebra, extending some ideas in the mathematical physics literature.
item.dc:creator: Vin\'icius Bernardes, Theodore Erler, Atakan Hilmi F{\i}rat, Igor Khavkine

item.title: Effects of Solar Wind Plasma Noise on Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background Searches with a Space Based Interferometer Network
item.description: arXiv:2607.05368v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The LISA-Taiji dual detector network improves millihertz SGWB sensitivity through cross correlation measurements. Solar wind plasma, however, can generate plasma noise correlated between detectors and bias SGWB cross correlation estimates. We use high time resolution electron density data from Wind/SWE, estimate the solar wind electron density fluctuation spectrum with the Lomb-Scargle method, and propagate the resulting plasma noise to the TDI A/E channels of the LISA-Taiji network. By including finite arm propagation, Taylor frozen flow spatial correlations, and the network overlap reduction response, we compute the SGWB parameter bias induced by interdetector plasma noise. Although the single detector plasma residual is below the reference noise, the component correlated between detectors can enter the SGWB cross correlation estimator directly. Under dual detector scale coverage, the plasma induced parameter bias for a power law SGWB can reach $12.73\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty. For M2/M3 cosmic string spectra, the bias in $\ln G\mu$ can reach $19.26\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty for the network configurations, observing times, and frequency bands considered here. These results show that the impact of solar wind plasma noise cannot be assessed from the single detector residual noise level alone. In LISA-Taiji SGWB searches, the interdetector correlated component of this noise can directly affect parameter estimation.
item.dc:creator: Mengfei Sun, Borui Wang, Jie Wu, Jin Li, Shengyi Ye

item.title: Residual Galactic binary foreground in LISA stochastic gravitational-wave background inference: source power concentration and spectral degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2607.25349v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Galactic compact binaries are expected to form a dominant millihertz foreground for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), and residual foreground power can bias stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) inference or increase its uncertainty. Using the LISA Data Challenge 2A (LDC2A) injections and the Erebor injection-recovery match, we construct a catalog residual spectrum from 0.4 to 6.0 mHz. We distinguish two effects. The first is the departure from Gaussianity of a sum of source signals with independent random phases, quantified by its excess kurtosis; the second is the spectral degeneracy between the residual and the SGWB in the mean binned power. Source discreteness determines the excess kurtosis of this sum, but instrumental noise and fiducial SGWB power strongly reduce its magnitude in most bins. We quantify this degeneracy with a local Fisher information matrix for the SGWB amplitude $\Omega_0$ and the residual-power factor $\beta$. For a frequency-independent SGWB with $\Omega_0=10^{-11}$ and residual power distributed uniformly over the Fourier frequencies within each bin, marginalizing over $\beta$ increases the $\Omega_0$ uncertainty by $13.6\%$ with the Gaussian Fourier-amplitude covariance and by $13.8\%$ with the finite-source diagonal random-phase covariance. Under the Gaussian Fourier-amplitude covariance, the largest allowed prior standard deviation on $\beta$ that limits this increase to $10\%$ is $0.0073$. With this covariance recomputed at each fiducial amplitude, the uncertainty increase ranges from $12.7\%$ to $20.7\%$ over $10^{-13}\leq\Omega_0\leq10^{-10}$. The residual-SGWB spectral degeneracy persists under alternative distributions of residual power over Fourier frequencies and diagonal covariances, while omitting the residual induces a systematic bias in the fitted SGWB amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Ruo-Yu Guan, Yan Wang

item.title: Perturbative Dissipation in Minimal Warm Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2608.08345v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an analysis of the perturbative modes of dissipation in the minimal warm inflation model where an axion-inflaton is coupled to a gluon thermal bath through the axion-gauge coupling. The corresponding friction coefficient, which generically is governed by IR physics, for the processes we consider is dominated by Landau damping of soft space-like gluons and the plasmon decay of hard on shell gluons. Since both of these processes are IR dominated, the friction coefficient becomes sensitive to the non-perturbative magnetic mass scale $m_{g}^{-1} \sim (\alpha T)^{-1}$ which in turn leads to the friction coefficient's overall linear proportionality to $\alpha$, which is much less suppressed in $\alpha$ powers compared to the well understood term from Chern-Simons (CS) diffusion $(\propto \alpha^5)$. On the other hand, this contribution to the friction coefficient is suppressed due to slow roll. We show that this can be viewed as a suppression of local spontaneous CPT violation for derivative couplings in general and that time correlations of nonlocal variables which do not fall off at large time separations are what allow an unsuppressed friction coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Daniel J. H. Chung, Nidhi Sudhir, Lian-Tao Wang

item.title: A Note on a High-Energy Limit of Gravitational Perturbation Theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.19941v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The post-Minkowskian expansion of general relativity expands the metric in Newton's constant G around flat space-time, but much effort currently focuses on ways to extend its range of applicability by summing the perturbative series to all orders. A regime of particular interest is a specific high-energy limit where a formula derived recently provides the momentum kick of binary scattering problem to all orders, and even suggests an approach towards strong coupling. We show that this is an asymptotic expansion. Although the series diverges we give evidence that it is Borel summable, and the full function in integral form is finite. As a by-product we determine the transcendentality properties of the coefficients in the expanded expression.

item.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
item.description: arXiv:2609.40068v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.

item.title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
item.description: arXiv:2609.40315v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. item.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
item.description: arXiv:2610.14806v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength ($\alpha$). The effective lifetime of the sound-wave source increases for slower PTs, decreasing for faster PT with larger $\beta/H$ and rising with smaller $\alpha$. While the simulated amplitude of normalized gravitational waves is of order $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$, in alignment with Minkowski-spacetime results, the resulting GW spectra differ markedly from those scenarios.

item.title: Black Hole Entropy from Entangled Quantum Reference Frames
item.description: arXiv:2610.37750v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the extended phase space of Donnelly and Freidel, the edge modes of a Schwarzschild black hole are dynamical reference frames whose phase space is the cotangent bundle of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Gluing the two exterior regions at the bifurcation point leaves a single canonical pair. Within the extended phase space, this pair can be described either by Kucha\v{r}'s mass and difference of asymptotic times or by the area and the relative rapidity of the two frames, which are two gauge choices of the same system. The latter is the pair of Carlip and Teitelboim, and the relative rapidity is the time shift of the crossed product construction. We quantize the frames in this gauge and construct the gravitational entangling product of the two exteriors. Requiring the frames to be causal restricts them to the semigroup $\mathrm{SL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, whose Plancherel measure yields the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as the entanglement entropy between the two exteriors, together with a logarithmic correction, both independent of the ultraviolet cutoff.

item.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04441v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) inflation. We construct the Hamiltonians from the quadratic actions and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing parameters. Although the tensor propagation speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We then calculate the Nielsen circuit complexity of the corresponding two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation between the squeezing amplitudes, while the squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Therefore, the circuit complexity is mainly controlled by the evolution of the squeezing amplitudes. For the benchmark parameters considered here, a positive coupling increases the preparation cost of the scalar Gaussian state but slightly decreases that of the tensor Gaussian state. The scalar sector is therefore more sensitive to the GB coupling, whereas the luminal tensor sector provides a cleaner probe of the pump-field mechanism. Their opposite responses provide a differential state-space diagnostic of the same EGB background.
